title: Query-Based Black-Box Stealthy Sensor Attacks on Cyber-Physical Systems
problem: Designing stealthy sensor attacks on cyber-physical systems under black-box conditions (minimal knowledge of target system) requires maintaining attack stealthiness both in output (avoiding detector alerts) and during attack generation (limiting detector queries).
motivation: CPS are deployed in safety-critical domains (financial fraud detection, power grids) but are vulnerable to adversarial sensor spoofing that evades traditional monitoring, requiring study of attack vectors to improve defense mechanisms.
method: Query-based black-box attack framework using active learning to extract detector information into a time series model without triggering alerts. The framework maintains stealthiness during training via adaptive query budgeting and generates attack sequences from the learned model that bypass CPS safety constraints.
key_novelty: First active learning method for stealthy sensor attacks that maintains both output-level and query-level stealth by learning detector behavior through constrained queries and generating attacks from the learned model.
contributions: Query-based black-box attack framework with adaptive query budgeting for stealthiness.
Active learning method to extract detector dynamics without triggering alerts.
Time series model-based attack generation maintaining safety violations while evading detection.

metrics.other: effectiveness demonstrated on 4 numerical simulations and high-fidelity simulator

primary_theme: stealthy adversarial sensor attacks on cyber-physical systems
